solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: A small cup is returned to old box in May perhaps

parts.note: a cup won in competition is a trophy

indicators.note: returned means the little word is is turned back to front

parts.note: a cist is an ancient stone burial box or coffin

explanation.surface: Someone fetches a little cup from storage and puts it back in an antique chest, perhaps in the month of May.
explanation.walkthrough: 'May' poses as the month but is Brian May, Queen's guitarist, who holds a doctorate in the subject; 'returned' turns IS into SI.
explanation.definitionFit: Brian May is an example: the rock guitarist completed a PhD studying interplanetary dust in the solar system.

clue.text: Patsy invests a small stake in second film

indicators.note: invests means clothes or surrounds, so the film wraps the stake

parts.note: a coat is a thin film or layer
a peg is a small stake driven into the ground

explanation.surface: A dupe puts a modest sum into a sequel movie.
explanation.definitionFit: A patsy is a person made to take the blame for others, a synonym.

clue.text: Dance with odd beat every now and then

parts.note: rum is an old-fashioned word for odd or strange

indicators.note: every now and then picks alternate letters of beat

explanation.surface: A dance with a strange rhythm that only appears occasionally.
explanation.definitionFit: A Cuban ballroom dance, one example of the general term.

clue.text: He objects to badger being fed rubbish

indicators.note: being fed means the nagging word takes the rubbish inside it

parts.note: to badger is to pester
rot means nonsense or rubbish

explanation.surface: Someone complains about a badger being given scraps to eat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'badger' looks like the animal but is the verb to nag.
explanation.definitionFit: A demonstrator is a person who objects, voicing opposition in public.

clue.text: Precision soars after scrapping vehicle plant

indicators.note: after scrapping means the vehicle is taken out
soars, going upward in a down clue, means the word is read bottom to top

parts.note: accuracy means precision
a car is a vehicle

explanation.surface: Precision rises once a vehicle factory is scrapped.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'soars' means read upwards; 'plant' looks like the factory of the surface but is the botanical sense.
explanation.definitionFit: A yucca is an evergreen shrub with sword-shaped leaves, so an example of a plant.

clue.text: Untruthful couples used to live here before nursing college

indicators.note: nursing means holding, so C sits within the pieces

parts.note: unmarried couples sharing a home were said to be living in sin
ere is an old word for before

explanation.surface: Lying couples once lived in a place before they cared for a college.
explanation.walkthrough: C goes between IN SIN and ERE.
explanation.definitionFit: Insincere and untruthful both describe someone not saying what they really mean.

clue.text: Actor's clubs

definitions.meaning: golf clubs with angled metal heads are named after the metal they were made of

explanation.definitionFit: Jeremy Irons is a stage and film actor; a golfer's set includes several metal-headed clubs.

clue.text: He's left Will close to vast demesne

indicators.note: close to means the end letter of vast

parts.note: a demesne is land held as an estate

explanation.surface: A man called Will has left, near a huge country property.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Will' looks like a name; it is a legal will.
explanation.definitionFit: A testate is a person who dies having made a valid will, legal language.

clue.text: Notice indicating location of bookmaker's ball?

parts.note: SP is starting price, the odds a bookmaker offers at the off
a sign saying here shows where something is

explanation.surface: A sign showing where a bookie's ball can be found.
explanation.walkthrough: The notice reads 'SP here', as if pointing to the bookmaker's starting prices.
explanation.definitionFit: A sphere is a perfectly round solid, the shape of a ball.

clue.text: Parish singers always love music, primarily church music

indicators.note: primarily asks for the leading letter of each of the five words before it

explanation.surface: A parish choir is devoted above all to the music of the church.
explanation.definitionFit: A biblical song from the Book of Psalms, sung or chanted as part of worship.

clue.text: Causes hole in footwear heading off

indicators.note: in tells us the hole goes inside the shortened footwear
heading off says the first letter of the footwear is dropped

parts.note: moccasins are soft leather slip-on shoes
O, shaped like a ring, stands for a hole

explanation.surface: A hole in a shoe makes trouble for someone setting off on a walk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heading off' removes M from MOCCASINS, leaving OCCASINS; O then goes in.
explanation.definitionFit: To occasion something is to bring it about, a formal verb synonym for causes.

clue.text: Lift European tax shelter controls

indicators.note: controls here means holds or contains, so the shelter wraps round the tax

parts.note: the lee is the sheltered side, away from the wind
VAT is value added tax, the UK sales tax

explanation.surface: A European tax haven is said to keep its own levies under control.
explanation.definitionFit: To lift something is to raise it up, a plain verb synonym.

clue.text: State in which men get confused, incontinent?

indicators.note: in which tells us the jumbled men are placed inside the continent

parts.note: read as in continent: Asia is the largest continent, and the in also marks the placing

indicators.note: get confused tells us the letters of men are mixed up

explanation.surface: A sly question about a condition where men become muddled and lose bladder control.
explanation.walkthrough: 'incontinent' looks like the medical word but splits as 'in continent'; the confusion in the surface also hints at the memory loss itself.
explanation.definitionFit: Loss of memory is a condition or state a person can be in.

clue.text: Devour over half of book in vessel

indicators.note: over means the eating word sits over, enclosing, the half book

parts.note: to devour is to eat greedily

indicators.note: half of takes the first two of the four letters of book

explanation.surface: A reader in a boat gulps down half a novel.
explanation.definitionFit: An E-boat was a German fast torpedo boat of the Second World War, a type of vessel.

clue.text: Use it to fly-fish endlessly for profit at first

indicators.note: endlessly means the fish loses its final letter

parts.note: turbot is a flat sea fish
pro means for, in favour of

indicators.note: at first takes the opening letter of profit

explanation.surface: Fly-fishing done without end, to make money from the start.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fly-fish' splits: 'fly' ends the definition and 'fish' starts the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A turboprop is an aircraft engine, a jet turbine driving a propeller, used for flight.

clue.text: Noted horse owner in furious race with poet over miles

indicators.note: over means the jumbled words cover, sitting round, the abbreviation for miles
furious suggests wild disorder, so race and poet are scrambled

explanation.surface: A well-known racehorse owner is enraged by a contest that pits him against a poet over distance.
explanation.walkthrough: Tom Pearce lends his grey mare in the English folk song 'Widecombe Fair'.
explanation.definitionFit: In the old Devon folk song, Tom Pearce owns the grey mare borrowed for the ride to the fair.

clue.text: Lad's briefly into rock music, in charge of generating energy

indicators.note: into means the shortened lad goes inside the music

parts.note: metal is heavy rock music

indicators.note: briefly means the word for lad is cut short

parts.note: a lad is a boy; the 's is is, a link

explanation.surface: A young man is getting into rock music, and is in charge of producing power.
explanation.definitionFit: Metabolism is the body's process of turning food into energy, so the adjective relates to that.

clue.text: Gunners taking a bath or shower?

parts.note: RA is the Royal Artillery, the gunners
someone taking a bath is in water

explanation.surface: Soldiers deciding whether to have a bath or a shower.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shower' is a fall of rain, not a wash.
explanation.definitionFit: Water that falls in a rain shower is precisely this.

clue.text: Crack team, mostly attractive

parts.note: Inter is Internazionale, the Milan football club

indicators.note: mostly says the word for attractive loses its ending

parts.note: attractive means pretty

explanation.surface: A first-rate side, most of them good-looking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mostly' here takes off two letters, TY, rather than the usual one.
explanation.definitionFit: To crack a code is to decipher or make sense of it, which is what interpreting does.

clue.text: Sort of socialist, extremely liberated type

indicators.note: sort of signals that the letters of socialist are reworked
liberated means freed of some letters, which leave the jumble

parts.note: so means extremely, as in so good

explanation.surface: A kind of left-winger, extremely free.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove S and O from SOCIALIST and rearrange the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: Italics are a sloping style of printing type.

clue.text: She showed some initiative after revolution

indicators.note: after revolution means that part is read backwards
some means only part of the word initiative is used

explanation.surface: A woman displayed a bit of drive once the uprising had happened.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters ATIVE end 'initiative'; turned round they read the name. The surface fits Eva Perón's rise in Argentina.
explanation.definitionFit: Eva Perón is the woman put on show in the Lloyd Webber and Rice stage musical named after her.

clue.text: A racket, say, and what it does

indicators.note: say tells us the phrase is to be heard rather than read

parts.note: a racket is a din, a noise

explanation.surface: A tennis racket, for example, and what it is used for.
explanation.walkthrough: 'racket' looks like the tennis bat but means a din.
explanation.definitionFit: A loud din irritates those near it, which is what this verb describes.

clue.text: Designer genes backfired in robot

indicators.note: backfired means the two pieces are read back to front

parts.note: Christian Dior was a famous fashion designer
DNA is the molecule that carries genes

explanation.surface: Engineered genes went wrong inside a machine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Designer genes' looks like genetic engineering; it is DIOR then DNA, and DIORDNA reversed spells the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: An android is a robot built to look and act like a human being.

clue.text: Drunk is necking quietly during party

indicators.note: during means the inner pieces come within the party

parts.note: a do is a party

indicators.note: necking means swallowing, so is takes the quiet letter inside

parts.note: P is piano, the musical marking for quiet

explanation.surface: A drunk is kissing discreetly at a party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'necking' looks like kissing but means swallowing.
explanation.definitionFit: A dipso, short for dipsomaniac, is a slang word for a heavy drinker.

clue.text: Consent to plan to abandon Sweden

indicators.note: to abandon means the abbreviation for Sweden is left out

parts.note: a design is a plan
S is the international vehicle code for Sweden

explanation.surface: Agreeing to a plan to leave Sweden.
explanation.definitionFit: To deign is to condescend, grudgingly agreeing to do something beneath one.

clue.text: Smooth victory in Stanley

parts.note: a bald head is smooth and hairless
a victory is a win

explanation.surface: An easy win for someone called Stanley.
explanation.walkthrough: Stanley Baldwin was a British Conservative prime minister between the world wars.
explanation.definitionFit: Stanley is the first name of the interwar Conservative prime minister, so the forename stands for the surname.

clue.text: Brand new way to start networking?

parts.note: a logo is a brand's symbol

explanation.surface: A fresh brand might be the way to begin making business contacts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'networking' suggests meeting people; here it is a computer network.
explanation.definitionFit: Entering a username and password to begin a computer session is how one joins a network.

clue.text: Just one priest stops fighting

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: stops means plugs a gap, so the priest sits inside the fighting word

parts.note: martial means relating to fighting or war

explanation.surface: A lone cleric puts an end to the conflict.
explanation.definitionFit: Just and fair-minded mean not taking sides, so the two adjectives are synonyms.

clue.text: Crude tycoon, say, rebutted Times leader of yesterday

indicators.note: rebutted, pushed back, means the abbreviation for say is reversed

parts.note: e.g., for example, is what say means
T is the abbreviation for time, so times gives two of them

indicators.note: leader of takes the first letter of yesterday

explanation.surface: An oil baron rejects what the Times newspaper said in yesterday's editorial.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Crude' is crude oil, not rude; J Paul Getty made his fortune from oil.
explanation.definitionFit: J Paul Getty was an American oil billionaire, so a magnate of crude petroleum.

clue.text: It's bustling at weekend, yet implicitly very quiet

definitions.meaning: a mall is busy with crowds on Saturdays and Sundays
the centre of the word shopping is PP, pianissimo, the musical marking for very quiet

explanation.surface: A place is crowded on Saturdays, yet in a hidden way it is extremely peaceful.
explanation.walkthrough: The second reading takes the phrase literally: the middle two letters of 'shopping' are PP, which in music means very quiet.
explanation.definitionFit: A mall full of stores is at its busiest when people are off work.
